docs.title: CytoMetrics
docs.text:
CytoMetrics is a Karcytics plugin that finds cells in microscopy images and measures them. It segments cells with Cellpose-SAM or classical image processing (Otsu thresholding, marker-based watershed), then reports area, perimeter, circularity and diameter for each cell, with a histogram, a sortable table and CSV export.

  • New here? Start with Getting Started.
  • Publishing results? See How to Cite: CytoMetrics stands on published scientific work, and the authors deserve the credit.
  • Contributing? Read the Architecture Overview and the Expansion Plan, which describes where the plugin is going: per-channel intensity, image cytometry with gating, batch runs, and assay modes such as colony counting and viability.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: CytoMetrics runs as an isolated Karcytics plugin (process_model = "isolated"): the Hub starts ui_daemon.py under the plugin's own .venv interpreter and talks to it over msgpack frames on stdio. The plugin imports only karcytics_sdk, never the Hub's karcytics package.

docs.title: Today
docs.text:
src/karcytics_plugins/cytometrics/
  __init__.py            initialize(), get_panel_class(), __version__ (read from pyproject.toml)
  ui_daemon.py           daemon entry point (the SDK runtime pre-imports numpy)
  analysis/              no Qt
    model.py             ImageSet/Channel: files read via the SDK's read_image (native bit depth,
                         metadata pixel size and channel names), RGB composite
    units.py             µm vs px: a scale of 0 means uncalibrated and everything reads px
    state.py             CytoMetricsState (PluginState dataclass, saved in workflows; scale_source)
    pipelines/           otsu.py, watershed.py, cellpose_pipeline.py → list of cell dicts
  citations.py           verified Citation entries registered with the SDK
  report.py              methods paragraph + BibTeX sidecars for exports
  ui/
    main_panel.py        CytoMetricsPanel (PluginBase) + helper widgets and dialogs
    image_canvas.py      MultiChannelCanvas (zoom/pan, calibrate, draw, delete)
    channel_manager.py   channel table, asset import into the project
    workers.py           CytoPipelineWorker (AnalysisBase) + model download/library loading tasks

A pipeline returns [{"points", "area", "perim", "circ"}, ...]; the panel assigns IDs and stores them in CytoMetricsState.cells.

docs.title: Where it is going
docs.text: The Expansion Plan replaces the cell dicts with a label mask plus a pandas object table, makes segmenters and measurements pluggable through registries, splits main_panel.py into views, and moves code that other plugins also need (task helper, image reader, image view, citations registry) into the SDK. Read its §2 before changing main_panel.py: it lists the known duplication and design problems so new code doesn't add to them.

docs.text:
Folder Marker What Runs in tests/unit/ unit Headless analysis code: pipelines, image stack, state. No PySide6 widgets. pre-commit, CI (gates release) tests/functional/ functional End to end through CytoPipelineWorker, with real and fake segmenters CI (gates release) tests/integration/ integration, slow The real ui_daemon.py subprocess, via karcytics_sdk.testing.ui_daemon CI (gates release) tests/ui/ ui Widgets, offscreen Qt CI (informational, non-blocking)

docs.title: Fixtures
docs.text:
• tests/fixtures/images.py generates synthetic images (isolated discs, a touching pair, a border-cut disc, nuclear seeds) with known ground truth. No downloaded data, so no data licenses to track.
  • tests/fixtures/segmenters.py has FakeSegmenter, so tests never need the Cellpose model.
  • Real images may only be added to tests/data/ with a CC0 or CC-BY license recorded in tests/data/LICENSES.md.

docs.title: Golden values
docs.text: tests/unit/test_classical_pipelines.py pins today's counts and areas. If a change moves one on purpose, re-derive it and update the constant with the reason. Don't loosen it into a range. Known bugs are recorded as xfail(strict=True) tests, so fixing one makes the suite fail until the marker is removed.

docs.title: The real Cellpose model
docs.text: test_cellpose_sam_finds_isolated_discs is marked slow and skips unless ~/.cellpose/models/cpsam already exists. CI never downloads the model.

docs.title: Pre-commit and CI
docs.text: Pre-commit runs ruff, mypy, pip-audit, the license-compliance check (no GPL/AGPL/noncommercial-only dependencies under our PolyForm Noncommercial license), tests/unit, plugin signing, and (pre-push) security-ledger verification. CI repeats lint/type/audit/license, runs the release-gating tests on macOS and Windows, and runs UI tests without blocking the release.

docs.title: Plan: grow CytoMetrics from a cell outliner into an image-cytometry workbench
docs.text:
Status: Phases 0, 2–7 done; Phase 1 done except 1.7 (SDK release, waiting on the user). Phase 8 done except 8.10 (z-stacks, deferred). Paused before Phase 9 for the user's review. Resume from the first unchecked checkpoint in Phases and checkpoints.

Commits: everything goes directly on main in both Karcytics-cytometrics and Karcytics-SDK. No branches. One commit per checkpoint group (at least one per phase), conventional-commit messages.

Living document. Change it as we learn; record why in the decision log.

docs.title: 1. Why
docs.text:
CytoMetrics today: load images → calibrate → segment (Otsu / Watershed / Cellpose-SAM) → area, perimeter, circularity → table, histogram, CSV. About 3,200 lines, 1,782 of them in ui/main_panel.py.

The biggest gap is that it loads multi-channel fluorescence images but never reads a pixel intensity, and it truncates 16-bit images to 8-bit. The goal is a tool that turns any image into a table of objects (cells, nuclei, bacteria, colonies) with many measurements per object, then lets the scientist classify, gate, aggregate across conditions, and report with the methods text and citations written for them.

Image(s) ─► Segment ─► Measure ─► Classify / Gate ─► Aggregate ─► Report
           (pluggable)  (many features)  (rules / ML)   (well/condition)  (+ methods & citations)

Each use case is an Assay, a preset over those five stages. One plugin, several modes.

docs.title: 2.1 DRY
docs.text:
• Area/perimeter/circularity computed 4×: three pipelines plus _on_cell_drawn (own shoelace).
  • UI-param restore block pasted 3× (set_state, _refresh_table, _on_load_workflow). set_state also calls _refresh_table, so it runs twice.
  • Channel lookup and border exclusion repeated per pipeline. Diameter computed in both the table and the CSV export.
  • Task connect/disconnect boilerplate 3× in the panel. The same pattern exists in flow (6 files) and western-blot (3), so it goes to the SDK.
  • VRAM release in both panel shutdown() and module shutdown().
  • Copies of SDK code: FunctionalAnalysisTask (SDK FunctionalTask), SaveWorkflowDialog (SDK dialogs.py).
  • Version disagrees: __init__.py 0.2.2, pyproject.toml 0.3.2, README badge 0.2.2. The README and CLAUDE.md also still say "cyto3", but the code uses cpsam.

docs.title: 2.2 KISS
docs.text:
• Four names for one operation: export_state / load_state / load_workflow / apply_state.
  • set_state used as "refresh everything" after every small mutation.
  • Channel.path is monkey-patched and read back through three nested getattr fallbacks.
  • hasattr(self, "check_exclude_borders") guards on a widget that always exists.
  • The worker swaps the process-wide sys.stderr from a thread. Its signal has no listener, CellposeLogInterceptor is unused, and the progress bar never moves.
  • Save goes through the project manager; load reads raw JSON from a file dialog.

docs.title: 2.3 SOLID
docs.text:
• SRP: main_panel.py holds 8 classes. The panel owns layout, state, geometry, CSV, JSON, TIFF metadata, task orchestration and model management.
  • OCP: a new pipeline needs edits in four places, including "Cellpose" in text string matching on display names.
  • LSP/ISP: only Otsu inherits SegmentationPipeline; name is a property in one pipeline and an attribute in the others; get_parameters() is never called.
  • DIP: self.window().project_manager (works: the daemon runtime sets a RemoteProjectManager on the window, but the panel still reaches through its window for it); the panel edits channel_manager._add_row_to_ui and .table.cellWidget; the analysis layer returns UI-shaped dicts.

docs.title: 2.4 Correctness and performance
docs.text:
• Cellpose post-processing allocates a full-image array per cell (np.zeros_like(masks) in the loop), so cost is O(cells × pixels).
  • ~~Nested closures on task_scheduler signals run off the GUI thread~~: checked in Phase 1, not a bug (LocalTaskScheduler lives on, and emits from, the GUI thread). The closures were still replaced by submit_task.
  • A pipeline exception came back as {"error": ...} through finished and was shown as "No cells found". Fixed in Phase 1.2.
  • An uncalibrated manual draw silently uses a scale of 1.0.

docs.title: 2.5 Cellpose capabilities unused (installed: cellpose 4.2.1.1)
docs.text: Only diameter, channel_axis and flow_threshold are passed today. Unused: raw 16-bit input with the normalize options (percentile, tile normalisation), cellprob_threshold, min_size, max_size_fraction, niter, augment, batch_size/bsize, the progress callback, list input (batch), do_3D/z_axis/anisotropy/stitch_threshold, the flows output (cell-probability map → confidence), train.train_seg (fine-tuning), metrics.average_precision, io ROI and _seg.npy export, and denoise (Cellpose3 restoration).

docs.title: 2.6 Build and test gap vs. flow
docs.text: 2 test files vs. 106. No functional/integration/fixtures/data tiers, no license-compliance hook, no CI split between release-gating and UI tests, no matplotlib cache, no docs site, no .coderabbit.yaml.

docs.title: 3. Ground rules
docs.text:
1. SDK vs. plugin. Code goes in the SDK only when ≥2 plugins use it, now or as soon as it lands. CytoMetrics-only code stays local until a second user appears. Gating stays local: flow is independent, and CytoMetrics only writes the standard FCS format.
  2. SDK first. SDK changes land and get a version bump before the CytoMetrics commit that needs them; CytoMetrics then raises karcytics-sdk>=.
  3. Licenses: 100% sure or not at all. A model is adopted only when both its code and its weights carry an explicit license compatible with PolyForm Noncommercial (permissive: BSD, MIT, Apache). If the weights' license is unstated, the model is not shipped and the feature uses its fallback. check-licenses gates every commit.
  4. Cite in the app wherever applicable. Every segmenter, measurement family, assay and algorithm that rests on published work declares its citations. They show in the UI next to the feature and are written into every export (§6).
  5. Behaviour-preserving refactors are locked down by tests first (Phase 0 golden tests).
  6. Pre-commit gates commits. While iterating, run only the tests for the area being changed.

docs.title: 4. Target architecture
docs.text:
karcytics_sdk (shared)
  plugin/managed_task.py   FunctionalTask + progress_callback
  plugin/tasks.py          submit_task(task, state, on_finished, on_error, on_progress, on_cancelled) → TaskHandle
  contrib/imaging.py       ImageReader: bit depth kept, physical pixel size from TIFF/OME/ND2 metadata
  plugin/image_view.py     ImageView: zoom/pan/fit/drop/empty state/scale bar/calibration line, overlay layers (done)
  plugin/citations.py      Citation, CitationRegistry, methods-text + BibTeX writer, CitationsPanel widget
  cli: verify-ledger, check-licenses

karcytics_plugins/cytometrics
  analysis/                (no Qt; strict typing; fully unit-tested)
    model.py      Channel(name, data, color, path), ImageSet, Calibration, LabelMask
    session.py    AnalysisSession — single owner of images, masks, ObjectTable, params, history
    segment/      Segmenter protocol + registry; otsu, watershed, cellpose, colony, (gated) instanseg
    measure/      Measurer protocol → pandas columns; shape, intensity, texture, ratio
    table.py      ObjectTable (pandas DataFrame wrapper; CellProfiler-style column names)
    classify/     gates (threshold, polygon, boolean)
    track/        overlap/Hungarian linker, (gated) trackastra
    assays/       Assay protocol + registry; one module per assay
    batch.py      folder/plate runs, condition/replicate metadata, per-condition stats
    export/       csv, fcs, imagej_rois, cellpose_seg, report (methods + BibTeX)
    citations.py  CytoMetrics' Citation entries (registered into the SDK registry)
  ui/
    panel.py      thin: wires views to the session
    views/        mode_picker, setup, detect, review, measure, report, plate
    canvas/       CytoCanvas(ImageView) + layers + edit tools
    widgets/      hardware_monitor, histogram, scatter, inspector, numeric_item, wrapping_label
    dialogs/      model_center, validation_report
    params_form.py  controls generated from Segmenter.parameters()

docs.title: Phase 1: SDK shared foundations (Karcytics-SDK, then cytometrics adopts)
docs.text:
• [x] 1.1 FunctionalTask(progress_callback=...) (SDK 518e488). Delete cytometrics' FunctionalAnalysisTask.
  • [x] 1.2 submit_task(...) + TaskHandle.cancel()/detach() (SDK 518e488, 8ccd52b): one watcher QObject on the GUI thread, exactly one outcome callback, every connection removed however the task ends. Cytometrics adopted it. Flow and western-blot adopt it on their own schedule (out of this plan's scope).
  • [x] 1.3 contrib.imaging.read_image() (SDK 823010b): native dtype, canonical TCZYX, pixel size/z step/interval/channel names from OME, ImageJ, cm-unit TIFF resolution, ND2 (optional karcytics-sdk[imaging]). Inch-unit resolution is ignored on purpose (screen DPI). Cytometrics adopts it in 2.1.
  • [x] 1.4 ImageView (SDK a20e041): zoom limits, middle/Ctrl+drag pan (left-drag opt-in), fit, empty state, file drop, calibration line, scale bar, named layers. Cytometrics 9cd8f84 and western-blot f5d9f72 (on main, after fast-forwarding it to fix/theme-following) are built on it.
  • [x] 1.5 SDK citations + citation_widgets (a852509): Citation, registry, MethodStep, methods_text(), to_bibtex(), CitationLabel, CitationsPanel. Cytometrics registers verified entries, each pipeline declares citations + describe(), the Detect step shows a "Powered by" line for every algorithm, and CSV export writes _methods.md + _citations.bib (pulled forward from §6).
  • [x] 1.6 karcytics-sdk check-licenses (SDK acdbcf3); doctor now flags a repo with no license hook. Cytometrics' copy deleted. Not done for the ledger verifier, by decision: it is a stdlib-only script so CI can run it before installing anything (the CLI imports PySide6); its four copies are identical apart from formatting.

docs.title: Phase 2: domain model (cytometrics)
docs.text:
• [x] 2.1 analysis/model.py: Channel (native dtype, path, as_uint8() for display and the 8-bit OpenCV segmenters) and ImageSet (add_file via SDK read_image, get(name), composite() in RGB, size check). Multi-channel files take their names from metadata (OME/ND2) and colours from stain names (DAPI → blue, GFP → green, Cy5 → magenta, …). Only t=0, z=0 for now (3-D is 8.10). ImageStack and its 16-bit truncation are gone; Cellpose now gets native 16-bit data.
  • [x] 2.2 Calibration: pixel size from file metadata is applied automatically unless a scale is already set; the calibration line sets it manually; state.scale_source records which, and the methods text says so. Uncalibrated runs are allowed: every control, table header, CSV column and methods sentence reads px/px². Recalibrating converts already-measured cells.
  • [x] 2.6 Save/load through the project manager only: the SDK SaveWorkflowDialog, a 📂 Load Session button listing this project's CytoMetrics workflows (pm.workflows.list_all() → pm.load_workflow_payload). The duplicate dialog, the raw-JSON loader, the apply_state alias and the three copies of the UI-parameter restore are gone. CytoMetricsState.from_dict ignores keys it doesn't know.
  • Moved: LabelMask → 3.1, ObjectTable (pandas) → 4.1, AnalysisSession + state v2 migration → 5.1. They belong with the code that first needs them.

docs.title: Phase 3: segmenters, using Cellpose fully (cytometrics)
docs.text:
• [x] 3.1 LabelMask as the single source of truth (contours derived for display) and the Segmenter protocol (id, name, parameters(), citations, segment(ImageSet, params) -> LabelMask) + decorator registry. Otsu and Watershed ported; shared channel lookup and border exclusion. Done as analysis/segment/ (base.py: Param, Segmenter, SegmentationResult, @register, cells_from_labels; run_segmentation applies border exclusion and the area filter once for every segmenter). The label mask is the result; cell outlines/measurements are derived from it (still outline-polygon measurements until 4.1). Border exclusion is now a choice for every segmenter. Watershed seeds from distance-transform peaks (peak_local_max, new "Min. Cell Separation" parameter) and runs scikit-image's watershed, so a two-cell clump now splits without a nuclei channel (the strict xfail is now a passing test); it cites scikit-image.
  • [x] 3.2 Cellpose: raw 16-bit input with the normalize options (percentiles, tile normalisation for uneven illumination); cellprob_threshold, min_size, max_size_fraction, niter, augment ("High quality"), batch_size/bsize (memory). Done: all exposed except min_size (our area filter covers it) and bsize (fixed at 256 for Cellpose-SAM). normalize is always passed as a dict: passing a bool makes Cellpose 4.2 overwrite its module-level defaults. Every non-default setting goes into the methods text.
  • [x] 3.3 Progress: Cellpose's own progress argument only reports in 3-D, so segmenters report stages through a progress callback (model loaded, network run, then per-object measuring 90–100%), shown as a percentage on the scanning indicator. The stderr hijack, StreamCatcher and CellposeLogInterceptor are deleted.
  • [x] 3.4 Per-object confidence (mean cell probability inside the mask) from flows; confidence heat-map layer; "review uncertain" list. Done: Conf. column, mean confidence in the stats, outlines coloured red→amber→green, a cyan cell-probability overlay, and Next uncertain ▸ (least confident first, centres the canvas). Known layout glitch for 5.8: the histogram overlaps the Export header in a short window.
  • [x] 3.5 Fix the O(cells × pixels) loop (scipy.ndimage.find_objects / skimage.measure.regionprops).
  • [x] 3.6 Export ImageJ ROIs and _seg.npy (Cellpose GUI/Fiji/QuPath interop). Done in analysis/export.py, from the current cells (deletions and hand-drawn cells included): ROIs via roifile (BSD-3), _seg.npy with masks, outlines, ismanual, filename (flows omitted; optional for the GUI). Default names follow the image (<image>_rois.zip, <image>_seg.npy).
  • [~] 3.7 ~~Optional Cellpose3 denoise pre-step.~~ Dropped: Cellpose 4.2's denoise.py contains only the degradation helpers (add_noise) used to augment training; the restoration models (DenoiseModel, CellposeDenoiseModel) no longer exist, so there is nothing to adopt. Revisit only if a later Cellpose release brings them back.
  • [x] 3.8 params_form.py: controls generated from parameters() (basic/advanced). Delete the display-name string matching. Done: Param declares kind, range, unit (length/area, shown in µm or px, passed in px), advanced, enabled_by, help (tooltips). Values are remembered by key across algorithm switches. ui_params v2 = {pipeline: id, values}; v1 keys are migrated on load.
  • [x] 3.9 Each segmenter shows its citations ("Powered by …") in the Detect step.

docs.title: Phase 4: measurements (cytometrics)
docs.text:
• [x] 4.1 ObjectTable on pandas (add pandas) and the Measurer protocol + registry. Shape: area, perimeter, circularity, solidity, eccentricity, major/minor axis, Feret max/min, equivalent diameter. Done in analysis/measure/ (base.py Column/Measurer/ObjectView/MeasureOptions, shape.py, intensity.py, table.py measure_cells/rescale/write_csv). Cells are rasterised from their outlines and measured per bounding box (1,585 cells on a 2048² image in 0.6 s). The worker measures after segmenting; edits, background changes and reloads re-measure in a background task (newest result wins). Recalibration rescales lengths/areas without re-measuring. The area filter now uses the same pixel area that is reported. Min Feret uses rotating calipers on the hull of pixel corners (exact for rectangles).
  • [x] 4.2 Intensity per channel: mean, median, min, max, std, integrated; local-annulus or global background subtraction.
  • [x] 4.3 Texture (GLCM / Haralick, via scikit-image) and nucleus/cytoplasm ratio when a seed channel exists. Done: texture.py (6 CellProfiler-named Haralick features per channel, image-wide 8-bit quantisation, only in-object pixel pairs, 4 directions averaged) and nucleus.py (nucleus = cell ∩ above the nuclear channel's Otsu threshold; areas, N/C area ratio, per-channel nuclear/cytoplasmic means and ratio). Both are opt-in in the Results tab (the nucleus channel is picked there, independent of the Detect seed channel). Measurers gained optional enabled(options) and prepare(image_set, labels, options) hooks.
  • [x] 4.4 CellProfiler-style column names; units in headers (AreaShape_Area [um2] in the CSV, Area (µm²) in the table; tooltips carry the definitions).
  • [x] 4.5 Manual cells: polygon → mask → same measurers. Delete the shoelace copy.
  • [x] 4.6 Measurement families carry citations (Haralick 1973; CellProfiler naming). Crossref-verified skimage2014, cellprofiler4, haralick1973; the methods text adds a sentence per family used.

docs.title: Phase 5: UI overhaul (cytometrics, may grow as we go)
docs.text:
• [x] 5.1 Split main_panel.py: widgets/dialogs to their own files; panel becomes wiring only. AnalysisSession + CytoMetricsState v2 with a migration from v1 saved workflows. Done: ui/widgets/ (hardware monitor, scanning indicator, histogram, table items), ui/dialogs/model_manager.py; analysis/session.py (Qt-free: calibration, cells, delete/add, uncertainty, reload, methods, export names) with the panel delegating; state.migrate() turns v1 saves (display-name ui_params, per-cell area/perim/circ) into v2. The step pages (5.3) finish the split.
  • [x] 5.2 Mode picker ("What are you analysing?") → Assay selection; remembered per project. Done: a light analysis/assays.py (pulled forward from 8.1: id, name, description, steps, segmenter, Detect settings, measurement options, default stain) with Cells and Nuclei; ui/mode_picker.py cards; the choice is saved in the session (ui_params.assay) and remembered per project folder in the SDK PluginConfig (nothing written into the project). Restoring a session switches steps without overwriting its settings.
  • [x] 5.3 Stepper (SDK WizardPanel/StepIndicator): Load › Calibrate › Detect › Review › Measure › Report; steps supplied by the assay. Done with a local one-line StepBar + page stack + Back/Next (ui/stepper.py): the SDK WizardPanel paints every child and assumes one column, and its StepIndicator is vertical (≈180 px). Pages in ui/steps/ only build widgets; CytoMetricsPanel._wire() connects them. Report shows the live methods text (copyable) and the references (SDK CitationsPanel).
  • [x] 5.4 CytoCanvas(ImageView): layers (channels, masks, outlines, IDs, confidence), per-channel display range for 16-bit, colour outlines by any measurement. Done on the existing MultiChannelCanvas (no rename needed): per-channel visibility (checkbox in the channel table) and display range (Channel.display_range, auto = 0.1–99.9th percentile, display only), both saved with the session; outlines/IDs/probability layers toggle; "Colour outlines by" AI confidence or any measurement (viridis stops verified against matplotlib), with a legend.
  • [x] 5.5 Edit tools: delete, merge, split, brush add/erase, box-prompt re-segment (Cellpose on the drawn box), all undoable (SDK UndoHistory). Done: geometry in analysis/edit.py (rasterise → change mask → re-trace; merge bridges ≤2 px gaps and refuses distant cells; split cuts with a 1 px 4-connected line; brush-add keeps only what touches the cell), session operations, canvas tools (select/Shift-select, draw, split line, brush strokes, box), Merge/Delete selected, ↶/↷ + Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Shift+Z through PluginBase.push_state; runs, calibration and every edit are undo steps; a loaded session starts a clean history. Region runs keep cells cut by the box edge. Panel tasks are tracked and detached on close (a re-measure finishing after close used to hit a deleted table).
  • [x] 5.6 "Preview region": run the segmenter on the visible viewport only. Done: 👁 Preview on visible area draws dashed outlines on a separate layer; nothing is kept, a full run clears them.
  • [x] 5.7 Inspector: selected object's thumbnail, every measurement, confidence, flag. Done: the Cell tab of the results dock (widgets/inspector.py): thumbnail cut from the displayed composite with the outline, all measurements with units, source and confidence, 🚩 Flag (saved in the cell, Flagged column, dashed outline, undoable). Selection highlight is now white so it stands out over any colour-by.
  • [x] 5.8 Results dock: Table / Histogram (any metric) / Scatter / Plate / Methods & citations. Done (ui/results_dock.py): Table · Histogram (any metric) · Scatter (any two measurements; click a point to select its cell, canvas selection highlights points: the two-way link from 6.1) · Cell. Plate comes with plate layouts in Phase 7; Methods & citations live in the Report step rather than twice.
  • [x] 5.9 Model Center (replaces Manage AI): per model, size, license, citation, download/delete. Done: analysis/models.py (model registry with code/weights licences, source, citations; the excluded models and why, from §7) and ui/dialogs/model_center.py. Delete now removes only that model's file (the old dialog emptied the whole shared ~/.cellpose/models cache). The "Your models" placeholder was removed when fine-tuning was dropped (see the decision log).
  • [x] 5.10 Hardware monitor collapses into a status bar. Done: widgets/status_bar.py, one line under the steps (app/system CPU, RAM, GPU memory once torch is loaded; never imports torch).
  • [x] 5.11 UI tests for each view (offscreen): steps/picker (test_steps.py), editing/undo/dock (test_editing.py), images/calibration/measurements (test_panel_images.py), params form, canvas, Model Center, plus the Qt-free session/edit/measure units. 192 tests.

docs.title: Phase 6: image cytometry (cytometrics)
docs.text:
• [x] 6.1 Scatter of any two measurements, linked both ways with the canvas. Done: linking came in 5.8; 6.1 added log axes (shared ui/widgets/plot_axis.py), population colours and gate overlays. The histogram was rewritten the same way (numpy bins, log axis, gate markers).
  • [x] 6.2 Local gates: threshold, rectangle, polygon, boolean combinations; % positive; gate set saved with the workflow. Done: analysis/gating.py (Qt-free; also range and NOT; gates nest through parent; shape gates are tested in the log/linear space they were drawn in) and the Gate step (ui/steps/gate.py) driven by ui/gating.py: tools draw on the histogram/scatter, a population tree with counts, % parent and % total, exact cut-off editing, rename/colour/delete (dependants go too), Combine… dialog. Gates live in CytoMetricsState.gates (saved, undoable) and are described in the methods text (report.gating_step).
  • [x] 6.3 Population colouring on the canvas. Done: "Population" colour-by (deepest population wins; ungated grey), switched on from the Gate step; Okabe–Ito palette.
  • [x] 6.4 FCS 3.1 export of the object table (flow can open it, with no code shared). Done: analysis/fcs.py written from the standard (float32, $PnN = column, $PnS = label with unit, gates as 0/1 parameters); tests read it back with FlowIO (dev-only, BSD-3), the reader behind flow's FlowKit loader. fcsparser was not added: it pins numpy < 2. Also a population-statistics CSV and Gate_<name> columns in the cell CSV. Citation fcs31 (Crossref-checked).

docs.title: Phase 7: batch and conditions (cytometrics)
docs.text:
• [x] 7.1 Folder and plate-layout import; filename → well/condition parsing; metadata editor. Done: analysis/batch.py (Qt-free): find_images, parse_well, {field} file-name templates, plate layouts as a Well list or a plate grid, per-channel files grouped by the token that tells the typical image's channel files apart. The Batch step (ui/steps/batch.py, ui/batch.py) lists images with editable metadata and "Set condition…".
  • [x] 7.2 Batch runs, cancellable, resumable. Done: a Recipe (segmenter, params, channels, measurements, gates, scale) is taken from the current analysis; BatchWorker runs items one by one, writing each item's cells and table and the batch.json manifest after every item, so Stop + Run resumes. Changed settings ask before redoing finished items. "Open in editor" / "Save changes to batch" fixes one image. The batch reattaches with the saved session (CytoMetricsState.batch_manifest). Departure: Cellpose's list input isn't used: images go through one loaded model one at a time, which keeps per-image saving, progress and resume (list input would batch only the network, and hold every image in memory).
  • [x] 7.3 Per-image / per-condition stats with replicates; plate heat-map; comparison plots. Done: image_summary (count, count and % per population, mean of every measurement), condition_summary (images averaged within a replicate first; n = replicates, else images; SD and SEM), plate_matrix/plate_shape (6- to 384-well). Results dock Batch tab: Images table, Conditions (bar ± SEM/SD with replicate dots, beside the table), Plate heat-map (viridis, hover values, click a well).
  • [x] 7.4 Batch export (combined CSV/FCS + methods report). Done: cells.csv, images.csv, conditions.csv (every metric, long format), one FCS per image (metadata as CYTOMETRICS_* keywords) and methods/BibTeX (report.batch_methods: settings, gating, how conditions were summarised).

docs.title: Phase 8: assay framework and new assays (cytometrics)
docs.text:
An assay is a preset for one kind of experiment: which segmenter and settings to use, which steps to show, what to measure, what extra result to compute (CFU/mL, % viable, % positive, …) and what goes in the report and its citations. Each one is a card in the "What are you analysing?" picker. Cells and Nuclei (Phase 5) are the first two.

  • [x] 8.1 Assay protocol. Done: analysis/assays/: an Assay (segmenter, Detect settings, steps, measurements, picker group, citations, the word for one object) with an optional AssayAnalysis (its own settings, derived columns, suggested gates, headline results, overlays, actions such as "draw the counting area", methods text). A Results step shows the headline values as cards; batch runs add them per image as Result_<key> columns.
  • [x] 8.2 "Cells" assay = today's workflow, migrated.
  • [x] 8.3 Colony counter. Done: colonies segmenter (Hough dish, rim excluded, blur-subtracted flattening, polarity by skew, Otsu, distance-transform watershed); CFU/mL, countable-range warning (30–300), median diameter, plate coverage. Cites OpenCFU and Breed & Dotterrer 1916.
  • [x] 8.4 Nuclei / cell cycle. Done: DNA content (integrated intensity ÷ G1 peak × 2), Sub-G1/G1/S/G2-M/>4N with suggested range gates. Cellpose-SAM (InstanSeg not adopted).
  • [x] 8.5 Hemocytometer / viability. Done: trypan-blue darkness (1 − mean / local background), a counting-area box, cells/mL from chamber depth and dilution, calibration from the grid line spacing (autocorrelation of the line profile).
  • [x] 8.6 Transfection / % positive. Done: cut-off from a negative-control image (a percentile of its reporter intensity), a Positive gate, % positive.
  • [x] 8.7 Confluence / scratch wound. Done: texture segmenter (local SD, Otsu, small gaps filled); Confluence %; wound area, mean and narrowest width, closure against a start area set on the first image. The batch time course (closure over time per well) moved to 9.5.
  • [x] 8.8 Bacteria. Done: rods measurer (skeleton length, width with EDT correction, curvature, constriction, dividing flag).
  • [x] 8.9 Spheroid / organoid sizing. Done: spheroid segmenter (smoothing, Otsu, largest objects kept); diameter, area, volume π d³/6, circularity, solidity (Zanoni 2016). Growth over time moved to 9.5.
  • [ ] 8.10 Z-stacks: do_3D / stitch_threshold, volume measurements. Deferred (user, 2026-10-17: not a priority).

docs.title: Phase 9: time and interaction (cytometrics)
docs.text:
• [ ] 9.1 Time-lapse tracking: overlap + Hungarian linker (SciPy) by default; Trackastra if its weights-license gate passes (greedy/SCIP linking only, never Gurobi).
  • [ ] 9.2 Lineages, growth curves, division events.
  • [ ] 9.3 Click-to-segment with µSAM if its weights-license gate passes; otherwise the box-prompt Cellpose tool from 5.5.
  • [ ] 9.5 Batch time course: a {time} field in file names, results over time per well/condition, closure or growth relative to the first time point (wound closure, spheroid growth).
  • [ ] 9.4 Academy courses for CytoMetrics (SDK academy.py): "Count your first plate", "Gate GFP+ cells", "Score a scratch wound".

docs.title: 8. Decision log
docs.text:
• 2026-10-17: 8.10 (z-stacks) deferred at the user's request. The time-based parts of 8.7 and 8.9 (closure and growth over time in batches) moved to Phase 9 as 9.5, with the other time work.
  • 2026-10-17: the old Phase 9 (fine-tuning Cellpose-SAM, training sets, custom models, validation report, trainable live/dead classifier) dropped at the user's request: not enough annotated data to train on. The old Phases 8 and 10 merged into one Phase 8 (assay framework plus every new assay, colony counter included), and the old Phase 11 became Phase 9.
  • 2026-10-17: 3.7 (Cellpose3 denoise) dropped: removed from Cellpose 4.2 (only training-augmentation code remains).
  • 2026-10-17: Phase 3 keeps outline-polygon measurements so the golden values only move once, in 4.1.
  • 2026-10-17: the security-ledger verifier stays a per-repo stdlib script (CI runs it before installing anything); only the license check moved into the SDK CLI.
  • 2026-10-17: western-blot's local main fast-forwarded to fix/theme-following (one commit, no divergence) so its canvas migration could go on main.
  • 2026-10-17: one plugin with modes (Assays); pandas for ObjectTable; gating stays local (flow independent); SDK hosts only code shared across plugins; all commits on main in cytometrics and the SDK; only models whose code and weights licenses are confirmed; citations shown in-app and written into every export.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: Install CytoMetrics from the Karcytics Hub's Plugin Store. It runs in its own window and its own Python environment.

docs.title: Choose what you're analysing
docs.text:
When CytoMetrics opens it asks What are you analysing?:

  • Cells: whole cells in fluorescence or bright-field images. Starts with Cellpose-SAM and local background subtraction.
  • Nuclei: nuclei from a nuclear stain. Starts with Cellpose-SAM on the blue (DAPI/Hoechst) channel and adds chromatin texture.

The choice sets the steps (Load › Calibrate › Detect › Review › Measure › Report), the starting algorithm and the measurements, and is remembered for the project. Every setting can still be changed. To switch, click the analysis button next to the CytoMetrics title.

docs.title: Install the AI model (optional)
docs.text:
The Cellpose-SAM model (about 1.2 GB) is downloaded on demand, not bundled. You only need it for AI Smart Detect (Cellpose); Otsu and Watershed work without it.

  1. In the Detect step, click 🧠 Models to open the Model Center.
  2. Click ⬇️ Download. The card turns green when the model is installed.

The Model Center lists each model's size, the licences of its code and its weights, and the papers to cite. 🗑️ Delete removes only that model's file. It also lists models that were considered but not included, with the reason (CytoMetrics only ships models whose code and weights have a compatible licence).

The line under the steps shows CytoMetrics' CPU use, memory and, once a model is loaded, GPU memory.

docs.title: Load images
docs.text:
1. In the Load step, click ➕ Add Image Channel, or drop files onto the canvas. TIFF (including OME-TIFF and ImageJ TIFF), PNG, JPG and BMP are supported; Nikon ND2 needs the optional karcytics-sdk[imaging] extra.
  2. A grayscale file becomes one channel. A multi-channel file is split into one channel per stain, named from the file's metadata where it has names (for example "cells.ome.tif (DAPI)"). An RGB file is split into red, green and blue.
  3. Each channel gets a display colour from its name where the stain is recognised (DAPI/Hoechst blue, GFP/FITC green, mCherry/RFP/Cy3 red, Cy5 magenta). Change it in the Color column.
  4. Images keep their full bit depth: a 16-bit image is analysed as 16-bit, and only scaled to 8-bit for display. All channels must be the same size.

Only the first time point and z-plane of a stack are used for now.

Untick a channel to hide it. Select a channel to set its display contrast (the values shown as black and white, in the image's own units), or click Auto to stretch from the 0.1st to the 99.9th percentile. Contrast changes only what you see: detection and measurements always use the full data.

docs.title: Calibrate
docs.text:
CytoMetrics reports sizes in micrometres once it knows the image scale.

  • If the file stores its pixel size (OME-TIFF, ImageJ TIFF, a TIFF with centimetre resolution, ND2), the scale is set automatically when it loads. The Calibrate step shows "(from image metadata)".
  • Otherwise click 📏 Set Scale / Calibrate, drag a line along a scale bar, and enter its length in µm. A scale you set by hand is never overwritten by a later file's metadata.

You can also run without calibrating. Every size field, the results table, the CSV columns and the methods text then use pixels (px, px²), and an amber note on the Detect tab says so. If you calibrate afterwards, already-measured cells are converted to µm.

docs.title: Save and reopen your work
docs.text: 💾 (next to the title) stores the analysis (images, channel names and colours, scale, detected cells, settings) as a workflow in the open project. 📂 lists this project's saved CytoMetrics workflows; the Hub's dashboard can open them too.

docs.title: 1. Pick an algorithm (Detect step)
docs.text:
Algorithm Best for Method Basic Threshold (Otsu) Sparse, isolated cells on a clean background Global threshold chosen by Otsu's method. Touching cells merge into one object. Watershed (Clump Splitting) Clustered, roughly round cells Marker-based watershed (scikit-image). Splits touching cells from their shape, or from a nuclei channel when you turn one on. AI Smart Detect (Cellpose) Irregular shapes, faint extensions, crowded fields Cellpose-SAM deep-learning segmentation.

The Settings below the algorithm change with it. Hover over any setting for an explanation. Values you've set are kept when you switch algorithm (for example the channel and the size filter).

docs.title: 2. Settings every algorithm has
docs.text:
• Target Channel: the channel that outlines your cells.
  • Exclude cells touching image edges: cells cut by the image edge give wrong sizes, so they're dropped by default.
  • Min Area / Max Area: drop debris and merged clumps. Shown in µm² once the image is calibrated, px² before.

docs.title: 3. Watershed settings
docs.text:
• Use a nuclei channel + Nuclei Channel: a nuclear stain (e.g. DAPI) whose nuclei seed one cell each. The most reliable way to separate touching cells.
  • Min. Cell Separation: without a nuclei channel, two cell centres closer than this are treated as one cell. Start at roughly one cell radius; lower it if clumps stay merged, raise it if single cells are cut in two.

docs.title: 4. Cellpose settings
docs.text:
• Cell Diameter: typical cell diameter. Auto works for most images; set it if your cells are much smaller or larger than about 30 px.
  • Detection Threshold (Cellpose's cell-probability threshold, −6 to 6): lower it to find more and larger cells, including dim ones; raise it to keep only clear cells.
  • Shape Tolerance (Cellpose's flow threshold): higher keeps more, less regular shapes; lower keeps only well-formed cells.
  • Use a nuclei channel: gives Cellpose a second input channel.

Under Advanced settings:

  • Contrast: Low / High Percentile: the intensity range Cellpose stretches to before segmenting (default 1–99). Lower the high percentile if a few very bright cells wash out the rest.
  • Uneven Illumination: Tile Size: normalise contrast in tiles so cells in dark corners are found too. Try 3–5 cell diameters; Off by default.
  • High Quality (slower): test-time augmentation; runs the network on flipped copies and averages them.
  • Mask Iterations: raise it for long, thin cells (e.g. bacteria) that come out fragmented.
  • Largest Object: Cellpose discards masks bigger than this fraction of the image.
  • GPU Batch Size: lower it if you run out of memory.

Each Cellpose cell also gets a confidence: the model's mean cell probability inside its outline.

docs.title: 5. Run and review
docs.text: Click ✨ Run Segmentation; the button shows what it is doing (detecting, then measuring) and how far along it is. Cellpose-SAM takes tens of seconds on a large image (longer with High Quality on), and the first run also loads the model. To try settings first, zoom in on a typical area and click 👁 Preview on screen area: only the part on screen is detected, so it is much quicker; the result is drawn dashed and nothing is kept. Detected cells appear as outlines with ID numbers.

docs.title: Editing (Review step)
docs.text:
Pick a tool, then work on the canvas. Every edit can be undone with ↶ (Ctrl+Z) and redone with ↷ (Ctrl+Shift+Z).

Tool What it does ✋ Select Click a cell to select it, Shift+click to add more; drag to move around. Then ⧉ Merge selected (touching cells only) or 🗑 Delete selected. ✏️ Draw Outline a missed cell by dragging around it. ✂️ Split Draw a line right across a cell to cut it in two. 🖌 Brush + / 🧽 Brush − Paint pixels onto, or erase them from, the selected cell (set the Brush size). ⬚ Re-detect Drag a box: the current algorithm and settings run again inside it and replace the cells centred there.

Cells you've changed are marked edited in the Source column; they lose their AI confidence, since the outline is no longer the model's.

  • Right-click a cell to delete it straight away.
  • ✏️ Draw Cells (Manual) lets you outline a missed cell by hand.
  • Select a row in the results table to highlight that cell on the canvas.

docs.title: Reviewing Cellpose results
docs.text:
Each Cellpose cell has a Conf. value (0–1), the model's mean cell probability inside the outline. In the Review step:

  • Colour outlines by: AI confidence (red = uncertain, amber = borderline, green = confident) or any measurement (viridis: dark purple = lowest, yellow = highest; the range is shown underneath). Outlines and Cell ID numbers can be hidden.
  • Show Cellpose cell-probability map: a cyan overlay of where the model thinks cells are. Useful to see dim cells it nearly found (lower the Detection Threshold to include them).
  • Uncertain below + Next uncertain ▸: steps through cells under the threshold, least confident first, and centres each one so you can delete or keep it.

docs.title: Results panel
docs.text:
Under the steps, the results panel has four tabs:

  • Table: every cell and measurement; sort by any column; select rows to select cells.
  • Histogram: the distribution of any measurement; tick log for a log axis.
  • Scatter: any two measurements against each other, each axis linear or log. Click a point to select its cell on the canvas (Shift+click for more); cells you select on the canvas are highlighted in the plot. Once you have gates, points take their population's colour (grey: in no gate).
  • Cell: the selected cell close up: a thumbnail, every measurement, its source and AI confidence, and 🚩 Flag to mark it for later (flags are saved and exported in the Flagged column, and flagged cells have a dashed outline).

docs.title: 6. Gate populations (Gate step)
docs.text:
Gating sorts cells into populations by their measurements, the way flow cytometry does, for questions such as "what % of cells are GFP-positive?" or "how many large, bright cells?".

  1. In the Gate step, pick a tool:
  2. 📏 Threshold: click on the histogram where the cut-off goes. Cells above it are in the gate (switch to below under Selected gate).
  3. ↔ Range: drag across the histogram over the values to keep.
  4. ▭ Rectangle: drag a box on the scatter plot.
  5. ⬠ Polygon: click around a cluster on the scatter plot; double-click (or click the first corner) to close it. Esc or right-click cancels.
  6. The Populations tree shows each population's cell count, % of its parent and % of all cells.
  7. To gate inside a population (e.g. bright cells among the large ones), select it in the tree, then pick a tool: the plots switch to that population's cells and the new gate goes inside it.
  8. ∩ Combine… makes a population from two others: both (AND), either (OR), or not (every cell outside one).
  9. Select a gate to see it highlighted on the plots, type an exact cut-off, ✏️ Rename, 🎨 Colour or 🗑 Delete it (deleting also removes the gates that depend on it).

With Colour cells on the image by population on, each cell's outline takes the colour of the deepest population it belongs to; cells in no gate are grey. Gates are measured on whatever axis scale they were drawn on (log or linear), are saved with the analysis, follow undo/redo, and are described in the methods text.

docs.title: 7. Results and export
docs.text:
Every cell is measured from its mask, the same way whether it was detected, drawn by hand, edited or reloaded. The results table shows every measurement; hover over a column header for its definition. In the Measure step:

  • Intensity background: None reports raw intensities. Global subtracts the median of all pixels outside the cells. Local ring subtracts the median of a 5-pixel ring 2 pixels outside each cell, skipping neighbouring cells. Either adds Background and Corrected… columns.
  • Nucleus / cytoplasm from: pick a nuclear stain (e.g. DAPI). Each cell is split into nucleus (above the stain's Otsu threshold) and cytoplasm; you get Nucleus_Area, Cytoplasm_Area, Nucleus_NCAreaRatio and, per channel, Intensity_NucleusMean_…, Intensity_CytoplasmMean_… and Intensity_NCRatio_… (above 1 = enriched in the nucleus, e.g. for translocation assays).
  • Texture (Haralick features): six co-occurrence features per channel (Texture_AngularSecondMoment/Contrast/Correlation/InverseDifferenceMoment/Entropy/Variance_<channel>_3), at a 3-pixel distance, averaged over four directions. Slower on large images.
  • Distribution: pick any measurement for the histogram and its mean.

💾 Export to CSV writes one row per cell. Column names follow CellProfiler, with the unit in brackets (µm when calibrated, px when not; intensities in the image's native units, "a.u."):

Column Meaning ObjectNumber ID shown on the canvas Source auto (detected) or manual (drawn) Confidence Cellpose's mean cell probability (empty for other algorithms) AreaShape_Area [um2] Pixel count × pixel area AreaShape_Perimeter [um] Outline length AreaShape_FormFactor Circularity, 4π·area / perimeter² AreaShape_Solidity Area / convex-hull area (1 = convex) AreaShape_Eccentricity 0 = circle, towards 1 = elongated AreaShape_MajorAxisLength, MinorAxisLength Axes of the ellipse with the same moments AreaShape_MaxFeretDiameter, MinFeretDiameter Longest and narrowest caliper width AreaShape_EquivalentDiameter Diameter of a circle with the same area Location_Center_X, _Y [px] Centroid, in image pixels Intensity_Mean/Median/Min/Max/Std/IntegratedIntensity_<channel> [a.u.] Pixel statistics inside the cell, per channel Intensity_Background_<channel>, Intensity_Corrected…_<channel> With a background choice: the background level and the corrected mean and integrated intensity

With gates, the CSV has one Gate_<population> column per gate (True/False).

  • 📈 Export FCS 3.1: one event per cell and one parameter per measurement (plus a 0/1 Gate_<population> parameter per gate), as 32-bit floats. Open it in the Karcytics flow plugin, FlowJo or FCS Express to gate image data with flow tools. Parameter names ($PnN) are the CSV column names; the labels ($PnS) carry the units. Format: Spidlen et al., Cytometry A 77A:97–100 (2010).
  • 📊 Export population statistics: count, % of parent and % of all cells for every population.

Two more exports take your cells, as they are after your edits, to other tools:

  • 🔷 Export ImageJ / Fiji ROIs: a .zip of outlines named "Cell ". In Fiji: Analyze › Tools › ROI Manager › More › Open. QuPath can import it too.
  • 🧬 Export for Cellpose (_seg.npy): the masks in Cellpose's own format. Save it next to the image and open the image in the Cellpose GUI to keep editing; Cellpose can also train on it.

    • Every CSV and FCS export also writes a methods paragraph and BibTeX file listing the settings you used. When you publish results, cite the methods you used: see How to Cite.

docs.title: 8. Batch: many images, conditions and plates (Batch step)
docs.text:
Set the analysis up on one typical image first (Detect, Measure and, if you like, Gate). The Batch step repeats exactly that on every image: same algorithm and settings, same measurements, same gates, same calibration.

  1. Add images: 📁 Add folder… (every image directly in the folder) or ➕ Add files…. If your typical image was loaded as one file per stain (e.g. A01_DAPI.tif + A01_GFP.tif), files are grouped the same way: what differs between the stain files' names ("DAPI", "GFP") tells them apart.
  2. Say what each image is. Wells such as A01 or B3 in file names are found automatically. To read more from names, type how they are built in File names, using {well}, {condition}, {replicate} or any {field}: e.g. {well}_{condition}_r{replicate} reads B03_LPS_r2.tif as well B03, condition LPS, replicate 2. A 🧾 Plate layout CSV gives each well its condition, either as a list (a Well column plus Condition, Replicate, Dose, …) or as a plate grid (row letters down, column numbers across). You can also type into the list, or select rows and 🏷 Set condition….
  3. ▶ Run batch. Each image's results are saved as soon as it's done (in the project's CytoMetrics batches folder), so ⏹ Stop at any time and run again to continue. Images that can't be read are marked ⚠️ (hover for why) and the rest carry on. If you change the analysis after some images are done, you're asked whether to redo them.
  4. Check any image: 🔍 Open in editor (or double-click a finished image) loads it with its cells into the steps above. Fix cells in Review, then 💾 Save changes to batch.

Results are in the Batch tab under the steps:

  • Images: one row per image: its metadata, cell count, % in each population and the mean of every measurement.
  • Conditions: any of those per condition (or any other field): a bar for the mean with SEM or SD error bars, and a dot per replicate. With a Replicate field, images in the same replicate are averaged first and n counts replicates (biological replicates are the unit); otherwise n counts images.
  • Plate: a heat-map of any value by well; hover for the number, click a well to find its image.

💾 Export batch results… writes a folder with cells.csv (every cell, with its image's metadata), images.csv, conditions.csv (per-condition statistics for every value), fcs/ (one FCS 3.1 file per image, with the metadata as keywords, for flow software) and the methods text and BibTeX.

docs.title: 9. Assays
docs.text:
What you pick in What are you analysing? sets up the steps, the algorithm and the measurements. Assays with their own results add a Results step: the headline values as cards, the assay's settings, buttons for its actions and the paper behind the method. In a batch, every image gets the same values as Result_… columns, so they can be compared by condition and on the plate.

Assay Detects with Results Settings and actions Cells Cellpose-SAM size, shape, intensity of every channel Nuclei & cell cycle Cellpose-SAM on the DNA stain DNA content (2N = the G1 peak), % Sub-G1, G1, S, G2/M, >4N ✨ adds a gate per phase; set the G1 peak by hand if the automatic one is wrong Transfection / % positive Cellpose-SAM % positive, the cut-off, mean of positive cells add an untransfected image as the negative control (the cut-off is a percentile, default 99th, of its reporter intensity), then each sample Hemocytometer & viability Cellpose-SAM counted, live, dead, % viable, live and total cells/mL ⬚ Draw the counting area (cells whose centre is inside count) and add each square you count to the experiment; 📐 Calibrate from the grid (pick the grid line spacing); dilution, chamber depth; dead = darker than the cut-off (trypan blue) Colony counter finds the plate, evens out the lighting, splits touching colonies colonies, CFU/mL (warns outside 30–300), median diameter, % of the plate covered dilution factor and volume plated; add each plate of a dilution series and the countable ones (30–300) are pooled Bacteria Cellpose-SAM length, width and curvature along each cell's midline, % dividing ✨ adds a Dividing gate Confluence texture (cells are textured, the dish smooth) % of the image covered texture window about one cell wide; sensitivity Scratch wound texture, keeping the open gaps wound area, % open, mean width (area ÷ length), narrowest point, % closure add the first image as the start; later images (named by time or condition) are measured against it Spheroids & organoids smoothing and threshold, keeping the largest objects diameter, area, volume (π d³ / 6), circularity, solidity how many spheroids per image; a warning when a spheroid is too irregular for the volume estimate

Photo assays (Colony counter, Hemocytometer, Confluence, Scratch wound, Spheroids) work on one photo at a time: 📷 Load photo… shows it as it is, and loading the next one replaces it (and its objects). Analyse using picks the colour the detection looks at: Automatic takes the one where objects stand out most from the background (blue for cream colonies on yellow agar), or choose Red, Green or Blue yourself. The other assays load one image per stain, as in Detect.

Experiments. Most results come from more than one image: a sample against its negative control, the squares of a hemocytometer, the plates of a dilution series, treated against untreated cells, replicate fields of each condition. Analyse an image, then in Results › Experiment add it with its role (➕ Add this image as …); load the next image (🔄 Next image for stains, 📷 Load photo for photos), analyse it and add it too. The experiment's results appear as cards under the images, and the Compare tab under the steps overlays their distributions (or shows them as bars) with a row per image. Only the measurements are kept, so settings such as the cut-off percentile can still be changed; the experiment is saved with the analysis, and its method is added to the methods text. For many images analysed the same way, use the Batch step.

Assay Roles in the experiment What's compared Transfection negative control(s), named samples cut-off from the pooled controls; % positive, mean of positives and median fold change per sample Nuclei & cell cycle control, treated samples DNA-content profiles overlaid; % in each phase, change from the control Hemocytometer counted squares cells/mL from all cells ÷ all volume counted; precision ±1/√N; a warning when squares differ more than chance (χ²) Colony counter plates (each with its dilution and volume) CFU/mL from the plates with 30–300 colonies: Σ colonies ÷ Σ (volume ÷ dilution) Scratch wound the start (0 h), later images closure of each later image against the start Bacteria, Confluence, Spheroids images of named conditions replicates (same name) averaged with SD; lengths overlaid (bacteria), bars (confluence, volume)

Each object is named after the assay in the table and inspector ("Colony 3", "Spheroid 1"). The methods text and citations of each assay are added to every export.

docs.title: How to Cite
docs.text: CytoMetrics is built on other scientists' published work. If CytoMetrics contributes to your results, please cite the methods you used, not just the software.

docs.title: Always
docs.text: • Karcytics CytoMetrics, version from the Hub's plugin list. https://github.com/KalaimaranB/Karcytics-cytometrics

docs.title: If you used AI Smart Detect (Cellpose)
docs.text:
• Pachitariu, M., Rariden, M. & Stringer, C. Cellpose-SAM: superhuman generalization for cellular segmentation. bioRxiv (2025). doi:10.1101/2025.04.28.651001
  • Stringer, C., Wang, T., Michaelos, M. & Pachitariu, M. Cellpose: a generalist algorithm for cellular segmentation. Nature Methods 18, 100–106 (2021). doi:10.1038/s41592-020-01018-x
  • Paszke, A. et al. PyTorch: An Imperative Style, High-Performance Deep Learning Library. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 32 (2019). arXiv:1912.01703

docs.title: If you used Basic Threshold (Otsu)
docs.text: • Otsu, N. A threshold selection method from gray-level histograms. IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics 9(1), 62–66 (1979). doi:10.1109/TSMC.1979.4310076

docs.title: If you used Watershed (Clump Splitting)
docs.text:
• Meyer, F. Color image segmentation. International Conference on Image Processing and its Applications, 303–306, IET (1992). The marker-based (flooding) watershed.
  • van der Walt, S. et al. scikit-image: image processing in Python. PeerJ 2, e453 (2014). doi:10.7717/peerj.453. CytoMetrics uses scikit-image's watershed and peak finding.
  • Otsu (1979), above: Watershed uses Otsu's threshold to find the cell footprint.

docs.title: Measurements (always)
docs.text:
• van der Walt, S. et al. scikit-image: image processing in Python. PeerJ 2, e453 (2014). doi:10.7717/peerj.453. Shape measurements are computed with scikit-image.
  • Stirling, D. R., Swain-Bowden, M. J., Lucas, A. M., Carpenter, A. E., Cimini, B. A. & Goodman, A. CellProfiler 4: improvements in speed, utility and usability. BMC Bioinformatics 22, 433 (2021). doi:10.1186/s12859-021-04344-9. Measurement names follow CellProfiler.

docs.title: If you turned on Texture
docs.text: • Haralick, R. M., Shanmugam, K. & Dinstein, I. Textural Features for Image Classification. IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics SMC-3(6), 610–621 (1973). doi:10.1109/TSMC.1973.4309314

docs.title: If you used Nucleus / cytoplasm
docs.text: • Otsu (1979), above: the nucleus is the part of each cell above the nuclear stain's Otsu threshold.

docs.title: Classical image processing (Otsu)
docs.text: • Bradski, G. The OpenCV Library. Dr. Dobb's Journal of Software Tools (2000).

docs.title: Methods text written for you
docs.text:
Every 💾 Export to CSV also writes two files next to the CSV:

  • <name>_methods.md: a methods paragraph naming the software version, pixel size, the segmentation method and the settings you ran it with, with numbered references.
  • <name>_citations.bib: the BibTeX for those references, ready for Zotero, EndNote or LaTeX.

The Detect step also shows a "Powered by …" line with a link to the paper for whichever algorithm is selected.
